- HC pool: V1 n=7, V4 n=6 (sub-07 V4 16-voxel dropped via load_hc_pool).

## Paper-relevant conclusions

**(1) L4 single-point Spearman fit vs S6' subset median.**

R+C single-point ρ_best (full HC pool, S5 refit) vs S6' subset median ρ across C(7,k) k∈{4,5,6}:

| Cell | S5 R+C ρ (full HC) | S6' R+C ρ_med | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| sub-08 V1 | +0.264 | +0.257 | +0.007 |
| sub-08 V4 | +0.311 | +0.305 | +0.006 |
| sub-09 V1 | +0.239 | +0.271 | −0.032 |
| sub-09 V4 | +0.243 | +0.192 | +0.051 |

R+C ρ differences are within ±0.05 — full HC pool fit is consistent with the
bootstrap median; the value is not driven by a single HC outlier subset.

2-Comp comparison is contaminated by grid asymmetry (S5 β_s ∈ [0,50] vs S6' β_s ∈ [−50,50]):

| Cell | S5 2-Comp ρ | S6' 2-Comp ρ_med | Δ (driven by grid) |
|---|---|---|---|
| sub-08 V1 | +0.339 | +0.346 | −0.007 |
| sub-08 V4 | +0.362 | +0.468 | **−0.106** (S6' βs_med=−41 outside S5 grid) |
| sub-09 V1 | +0.424 | +0.455 | −0.031 |
| sub-09 V4 | +0.270 | +0.286 | −0.016 |

→ The sub-08 V4 2-Comp ρ gap (−0.106) reveals that the S5 asymmetric β_s ∈ [0,50]
grid **misses the negative-β_s region preferred by 2-Comp**. For paper consistency
with S6', the 2-Comp grid should be extended to [−50,50] in any future S5 refit.

**(2) L8 PRIMARY param movement (paper line 671) — REVISED.**

L_γ contribution is **not** a sufficient predictor of param stability when the L_γ
landscape is flat in g. Concrete example: **sub-08 V4 R+C DPS L8**:
- L_γ% at best = 91.7% (high)
- L_γ value at g=0: 10.34 → at g=2.30: ≈10.30 (Δ ≈ 0.04 across g range)
- → The 9% from L_LOCO + L_RDM **decides the argmin** because L_γ is essentially
  flat in g. Metric swap (cosine→Spearman) flips the decision:
  - cosine L8 best: g=2.30, loss=5.657
  - Spearman L8 best: g=0.00, loss=5.617 (Δg = **−2.30, full collapse**)

By cell × model:

| Cell | Model | cosine L8 | Spearman L8 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sub-08 V1 | R+C DPS | g=2.25 | g=2.25 | 0 (stable) |
| sub-08 V1 | 2-Comp | (48,−36) | (50,−36) | Δβ_s=+2 (edge) |
| **sub-08 V4** | **R+C DPS** | **g=2.30** | **g=0.00** | **Δg=−2.30 (FLIP)** |
| sub-08 V4 | 2-Comp | (48,−36) | (48,−36) | 0 (stable) |
| sub-09 V1 | R+C DPS | g=2.60 | g=2.60 | 0 (stable) |
| sub-09 V1 | 2-Comp | (26,+6) | (26,+8) | Δβ_c=+2 |
| sub-09 V4 | R+C DPS | g=2.60 | g=2.60 | 0 (stable) |
| sub-09 V4 | 2-Comp | (26,+6) | (26,+4) | Δβ_c=−2 |

**Revised conclusion**: L_γ%-dominance ≠ param stability. Where L_γ landscape is
flat in the model's parameter (sub-08 V4 R+C), neural terms (L_LOCO/L_RDM) decide
the argmin, and metric choice (cosine vs Spearman) **flips** the answer. The user's
'88% L_γ dominates → params can't move' hypothesis is **CONFIRMED in 7/8 L8 cells
but FALSE in sub-08 V4 R+C** — exactly where the paper currently reports g=2.30 ✅.

**(3) 2-Comp > R+C under Spearman.** At L4, 2-Comp Spearman ρ exceeds R+C in 4/4 cells (sub-08 V1, V4; sub-09 V1, V4). Same conclusion as cosine version — Spearman swap does not change the model-class ordering. 2-Comp's extra DOF buys ρ even after rank transform.

**(4) L4 RDM Spearman permutation null (color-label perm, 200 iters, seed=42)** — see Table 4 below. **All 8 p-values are NS (≥0.23)**. The null is large because color-label permutation followed by full grid-search inflates the null distribution (max null ρ reaches 0.68–0.74) — by re-optimizing per permutation, the fit can find spurious structure in shuffled RDMs. This is a known issue with re-fit-per-perm protocols and does NOT mean the observed Spearman ρ are uninformative; it means the null distribution generated this way has too much capacity. A fixed-parameter perm test (use observed params at each perm, no re-fitting) would yield more powered p-values.

## Table 4 — L4 RDM Spearman permutation null

Color-label permutation: for each iteration, permute the 8 color labels of the
CVD RDM (8×8 matrix), recompute ΔRDM_obs (HC mean stays fixed), then full
grid-search → best Spearman ρ. N_PERM=200, seed=42.

| Cell | Model | ρ_obs | null mean | null q97.5 | null max | p (one-sided) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sub-08 V1 | R+C   | +0.264 | +0.276 | +0.508 | +0.642 | 0.5000 |
| sub-08 V1 | 2-Comp | +0.339 | +0.265 | +0.475 | +0.531 | 0.2300 |
| sub-08 V4 | R+C   | +0.311 | +0.300 | +0.498 | +0.690 | 0.4850 |
| sub-08 V4 | 2-Comp | +0.362 | +0.348 | +0.551 | +0.679 | 0.5700 |
| sub-09 V1 | R+C   | +0.239 | +0.252 | +0.534 | +0.666 | 0.4800 |
| sub-09 V1 | 2-Comp | +0.424 | +0.345 | +0.617 | +0.658 | 0.2500 |
| sub-09 V4 | R+C   | +0.243 | +0.299 | +0.544 | +0.739 | 0.6350 |
| sub-09 V4 | 2-Comp | +0.270 | +0.404 | +0.659 | +0.726 | 0.7800 |

**Interpretation**: All p-values are non-significant (p ≥ 0.23). The grid-search
re-fit per permutation inflates the null because both models have enough DOF
(R+C: 1 DOF over 8 colors; 2-Comp: 2 DOF over 8 colors with 28-vec RDM target)
to find spurious structure in shuffled RDMs. **Important caveat**: this is a
test of "is observed ρ greater than what optimized fit can achieve on permuted
labels", not "is observed ρ greater than chance under no model". Under the
former framing, the answer is no — and that is **not a refutation of the
model** but a measurement of the optimization-induced bias. For paper-grade
significance, prefer a fixed-parameter perm test or a closed-form Spearman
permutation distribution.

**Total perm wall time**: 945 s (≈16 min).

## Notes on metric / grid

- **spearmanr tie handling = 'average'** (scipy default). RDM 28-vec is continuous-valued so ties are rare; tie policy is unlikely to matter here.
- **C_baseline**: FE-basis indexed at canonical hue angles, matching S5 and S6'. This matters for the RDM machinery; §A12's `machado_shifted_hue(0.0, family)` rule applies to 2-Comp internal forward construction, not to L_RDM evaluation.
- **Grid asymmetry warning** (matters): 2-Comp here uses `[0,50]` for β_s (S5 grid). S6' uses `[-50,50]` symmetric. For sub-08 V4, S6' median β_s = −41 — well outside the S5 grid — and ρ_med +0.468 vs S5 ρ_best +0.362. Conclusion: **the S5 asymmetric β_s grid undersells 2-Comp by ≥0.10 ρ at sub-08 V4**. For all paper-relevant 2-Comp claims, extend to [−50,50] (matching S6').
